summary: Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein rose from a violent rural childhood through CIA-backed Ba'athist plots to purge rivals, wage wars and gas Kurds, while writing propagandistic romance novels in his final years in power before his 2006 execution.

evidence.note: birth and contested childhood stories open the episode
CIA arms Ba'athists for the failed attempt on Qasim; later helps him flee
years of exile in Cairo after the failed assassination
1968 coup brings the Ba'ath Party to power
1979 purge of party rivals, executions taped and circulated
Kamel brothers defect to Jordan, then return and are killed
long reading of Zabiba and the King as allegorical propaganda
antisemitic plot of Begone Demons; uncle's anti-Persian, anti-Jewish pamphlet earlier
2003 capture, guards' account, execution in December 2006

notes: Format is deep-dive: the novels take roughly a third of the episode, the rest is biography. The transcript garbles the birth date; 1937 used. Iran-Iraq war, Anfal gassing and Kuwait are only brief mentions, so war and genocide themes and content warnings were left out. Scope kept national though Egypt and Jordan get short segments.
